SI-4_title.answer: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

NM2-1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression model was trained to predict voxel-wise gray matter volume (GMV) from age and sex in healthy controls, then applied to infer GMV deviations in OCD patients.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Following the previous studies (Marquand et al. 2016; Wolfers et al. 2018), we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict voxel-wise GMV from age and sex in HCs and then applied the trained model to infer GMV of patients with OCD.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.location: Han2023.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling latent disease factors

NM2-2_response_variable.detail: Gray matter volume (GMV) obtained using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis with CAT12 toolbox. Images were segmented, normalized to MNI space, modulated, and smoothed with 6-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.
NM2-2_response_variable.supporting_text: This framework obtained subject-level differences in gray matter morphometry measured with voxel-based morphometry analysis (VBM) using the normative model... We obtained GMV for each subject using the Computational Anatomy Toolbox (CAT12, http://dbm.neuro.uni-jena.de/cat12/).

NM2-3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as predictors in the Gaussian process regression normative model to predict voxel-wise GMV.
NM2-3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict voxel-wise GMV from age and sex in HCs
